correctness.rationale: For finite abelian A with N=|A| and char(F_q) coprime to N, Fourier inversion is valid over the algebraic closure and compatible with q-Frobenius descent. From e_x*e_y=e_(phi(x)+(1-phi)(y)) derive the known Fourier product hat(u*v)(chi)=hat(u)(Phi chi)hat(v)(Psi chi). The dual Psi has image I of size r=|(1-phi)A|, fibers of size f=N/r; Phi is a permutation. Each Frobenius orbit O in I of length d yields an fd-dimensional F_q block for coefficients of u on Phi(Psi^{-1}(O)); exactly one of q^(fd) assignments is zero, otherwise L_u rank increases by d. For R_u, nonzero u at image I contributes f rows per character and q^(N-r) free coordinates outside I, yielding the distinct right-rank polynomial. Summing q^(N-rank L_u) gives q^(N-r) product_O(q^d+q^(fd)-1), with 2q^N-1 trivial zero-factor pairs subtracted for both nonzero. Independent direct multiplication-matrix enumeration agrees with both rank polynomials and zero-pair counts in four prime-field cyclic examples; original script additionally covers F4 and noncyclic C3xC3. Modular characteristic excluded and rank invariance upon extension is justified by minors.
